title: Run
description: One run of a runbook on the daemon:its inputs as submitted, its confinement, where it stands and how it ended.

intake.description: The intake document itself, inline in the submit: text, at most 1 MiB.

context_path.description: The context directory the run reads (runbook run --context), under one of the daemon context roots; absent when none was given.

confinement_source.description: Where the level came from: the submit or the daemon's default. Absent for a run recorded before the daemon kept it.

autonomy.description: The level the run was submitted with, or took from the daemon's default; absent when none: every decision of the run waits for a client. Fixed at the submit and read from the record, never from the daemon's policy of the day.

decider.description: The kind of decider of the run, fixed like the level.

session_id.description: The session the run was submitted into; absent for a run of no session.

idempotency_key.description: The key the submit carried, when it carried one; a later submit with the same key returns this run.

serial_key.description: The serial key the submit or the delegation named, when it named one: the run waits (WaitingOnKey) while a run with the same key submitted before it holds the key: it is live, or the runtime took it up and has not let it go yet. Fixed at the submit.

key_wait.description: While the run is WaitingOnKey: `waiting on key <k> behind run <id>`, naming the newest run with the key submitted before it that holds the key (a live run, or a run the runtime took up and has not let go yet); absent in every other state. No command of the language sets it: the daemon derives it from the runs of the key when the view is read, so it names the run ahead of it now (a cancelled holder until the runtime let it go, then the one ahead of that).

ended_at.description: When the run left its last live state: ended, cancelled or failed to start.

outcome.description: Set when the run Ended; absent in every other state. Besides the outcome names of the runbook's protocol it holds the daemon's own causes: `orphaned` (the daemon stopped while the run was live and the runtime could not take it up again) and `runtime-failure` (the runtime failed after the run started), and `failed: step <action> <end>` (`<end>`: `exit <n>`, `signal <n>`, `timed out after <s> s` or `ended with no exit`) (the last program of the run's tree failed (it ended with an exit other than 0, was killed at its timeout or ended with no exit status, or Loom refused it for an exit its `exits.error` lists or a signal, an agent node (`sdc-node`) or any other program) and the tree has no other action to take; the event runbook.step-failed says why).

failure.description: Why the run failed to start; absent in every other state of the row. The view `run` also gives here what failed a run after it started: the reason of its run event `runbook.runtime-failed` or `runbook.step-failed`.

step_in_flight.description: The step whose program runs now, while the run is Running; absent otherwise (no program runs, the run waits, ended, was cancelled, or the daemon started again). No command of the language sets it: the daemon keeps it in its process from the run event `runbook.action-started` until the program ends, like the rows of Runbook, and a restarted daemon has none.

model_route.description: The route of the run's role `default`, the role a model process names when it names none of its own: the one the submit named, else the daemon's `route_policy.default`. Absent for a run that makes no model call (it has no model step: its runbook runs no agent node and no program whose per-call budget is above 0, and its decider is not a model above A0; a submit for such a run whose runbook runs programs and that named a route is admitted with none, and its first event `runbook.submitted` names that route under `model_route_not_taken` with the reason), for a run whose model calls come from its programs only that named none on a daemon with no declared `route_policy.default` or whose relay serves no run (a listener that is not loopback), and for a run of a daemon with no route. Always a route of the view Routes. Fixed at the submit; for a delegation the daemon classifies (path `classified`), set again with model_route_alias, model_route_source and model_routes when its run takes the route entries of the runbook the classifier picked, before that runbook's first model call.

model_route_alias.description: The gateway's alias of the model behind model_route, as the daemon's file declared it at the submit: what every call of the role names at the gateway. Absent with model_route.

model_route_source.description: The setting that chose model_route: run, protocol or default. Absent with model_route.

model_routes.description: The routes of the other roles of the run: those the submit named (`model_routes.<role>`) and those the runbook's route entries give; absent when there are none.

route_phase.description: The last phase the gateway gave of a route of the run that could not answer when the run was submitted: set when the run waits for its route (WaitingForRoute) and when it ends `stopped: route`; absent for a run that never waited.

path.description: For a run a Delegate created: how it became a run, read from its run events `runbook.delegated` and `runbook.delegation-resolved` (the path a classified delegation took when its run started); absent for any other run, and while the daemon classifies. No command of the language sets it.

protocol.description: For a run a Delegate created, once its path is taken: the protocol it runs, by the id its document declares (the named runbook, delegation-free, the runbook the classifier picked, or the id of the generated protocol). Read like `path`.

confidence.description: For a classified or generated delegation: the classifier's confidence, a number from 0 to 1. Read like `path`.

classifier_route.description: For a classified or generated delegation: the route of its classify and build calls (route_policy.classifier), by name. Read like `path`.

protocol_digest.description: For a generated delegation: sha256:<hex> of the protocol document the builder wrote, as the run took it. Read like `path`.

sdc.daemon.ConfinementLevel.title: ConfinementLevel
sdc.daemon.ConfinementLevel.description: How strongly a run is sandboxed, weakest first: the runtime's names. local is not confined; linux is. oci and pod are the runtime's planned levels and are not in the set until it offers them. A submit that names no level runs at the daemon's default level (runbook serve --default-confinement, or `confinement` of runbook.toml); a daemon with none refuses the submit by name and writes nothing, as the binary has no built-in default; the handler fills it. The daemon's floor is linux unless it is started lower; the default is never below the floor, and a daemon whose default is below its floor does not start. local must be asked for by name or set as the default, and is refused under a linux floor.

sdc.daemon.ConfinementSource.title: ConfinementSource
sdc.daemon.ConfinementSource.description: Where a run's level came from: submit (the client named it) or daemon-default (the client named none and the daemon's default level applied). There is no third source: a daemon with no default refuses a submit that names none.

sdc.daemon.ContextPath.title: ContextPath
sdc.daemon.ContextPath.description: A directory on the daemon's host, given as an absolute path. The daemon accepts it only when it lies under one of its context roots (runbook serve --context-root <dir>, repeatable; none given means no context from a path), and copies it into the run's workspace before the run starts: directories and regular files only, never an entry named .git (a directory, or the file of a linked worktree), never an entry of the exclude list (the daemon's `[delegation] copy_exclude`, default target/ and node_modules/, and the run's own workspace_exclude), within `[delegation] copy_max_entries` entries (default 50000) and `copy_max_bytes` bytes (default 268435456). A context over a bound fails the run's start `context-over-bound: ...` naming the bound, and nothing of it is copied (FailRunStart, outside the language); a copy writes the run event `runbook.context-copied` (record: exclude, the list it applied; entries and bytes, what it copied; skipped, the count of entries it left out).

sdc.daemon.DeciderKind.title: DeciderKind
sdc.daemon.DeciderKind.description: The name of a decider kind the operator configured (a table [deciders.<kind>] of runbook.toml): rule or model. A run names a kind, never a program or a path; a kind that is not configured is refused at the submit before anything is written.

sdc.daemon.DelegationPath.title: DelegationPath
sdc.daemon.DelegationPath.description: How a delegation became a run (docs/model-routes.md, section 9): named (it named a protocol, and that runbook runs with the request as its intake), free (the free run, one agent node whose instruction is the request, writing result.md: asked for by the protocol delegation-free, or taken by a delegation that names no protocol on a daemon without a classifier route), classified (it named none, and one call on the classifier route picked a runbook of the daemon at or above the threshold of confidence, 0.8) or generated (the classifier's confidence was below it, and one call on the classifier route wrote a protocol of the daemon's parts, which the loader accepted) or change (it named a repository of the daemon's runbook.toml, `[repositories.<name>]`: the protocol delegation-change, one agent node working in the run's worktree of that repository, whose change the daemon commits and pushes as the branch runbook/<run-id> when the run delivers).

sdc.daemon.IdempotencyKey.title: IdempotencyKey
sdc.daemon.IdempotencyKey.description: Optional text, at most 200 characters, unique per daemon, that a client sends to retry a submit safely: a second submit with a key already used returns the first run and creates none.

sdc.daemon.RoleRoutes.title: RoleRoutes
sdc.daemon.RoleRoutes.description: The route of each named role of a run (`writer`, `review`, ...) besides the role `default`: a role is the word a model process of the run names as its model, and the daemon's relay sends the call to the role's route. A role and a route are each one to 64 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`; a role does not start with `runbook-`, the prefix of the model the run's route file gives a role.

sdc.daemon.RouteName.title: RouteName
sdc.daemon.RouteName.description: The name of a model route the daemon declares (a table [routes.<name>] of its runbook.toml): one to 64 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. A client names a route by it, never by an address, a token or an alias; the address, the token file and the prices stay in the daemon's file.

sdc.daemon.RouteSource.title: RouteSource
sdc.daemon.RouteSource.description: The setting that chose a run's route: run (the submit named it, `model_route` or `model_routes.<role>`), protocol (the runbook's route entries, the file `bindings/<runbook>.routes.yaml` of format runbook.routes/1: the route its entry for the role names, or the route that meets the entry's needs; docs/model-routes.md section 2) or default (the submit named none and the daemon's `route_policy.default` applied; a daemon whose file declares no route but a lone `[gateway]` table and a model decider declares the interim route `default` on that gateway and takes it as its default, so a model run that names none says default too). The run's word comes first, then the protocol's, then the default.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.

sdc.daemon.RunOutcome.title: RunOutcome
sdc.daemon.RunOutcome.description: Open text: the outcome name of the runbook's protocol for the root case, or one of the daemon's own causes (`orphaned`, `runtime-failure`, `stopped: route`, `failed: step <action> <end>`). The run's state is the closed set; the outcome is not.

sdc.daemon.RunSettings.title: RunSettings
sdc.daemon.RunSettings.description: The settings of a run: a map from text to text (runbook run --set key=value), kept as written. Typed members come with the runtime's run-settings story; none are declared now.

sdc.daemon.RunbookId.title: RunbookId
sdc.daemon.RunbookId.description: The name of a runbook: a preset (sdc, sdc-bugfix) or the name of a runbook in the daemon's --runbook-dir.

sdc.daemon.RunbookVersion.title: RunbookVersion
sdc.daemon.RunbookVersion.description: The version of a runbook, as runbook list shows it. Optional in a submit: absent means the version the daemon has.

sdc.daemon.SerialKey.title: SerialKey
sdc.daemon.SerialKey.description: Optional text, 1 to 200 characters, that the submitter names (the daemon never derives one): runs with one key run one at a time, in the order they were submitted. A run whose key a run submitted before it holds is WaitingOnKey until no such run holds it: a live run holds it, and a run that was taken up holds it until its run thread in the daemon has returned, also after it was Cancelled; runs with another key or none are not held. A key that is empty or longer is refused before anything is written (400).

sdc.daemon.SessionId.title: SessionId
sdc.daemon.SessionId.description: The name of a session, chosen by the client that opens it.

sdc.daemon.StepInFlight.title: StepInFlight
sdc.daemon.StepInFlight.description: The step of a run whose program is running now: the action the bindings bind to the program, the case it runs for and when it started, the start the event `runbook.action-started` recorded. `seconds` is the time since `started_at` by the daemon's clock, read when the view is read.

action.description: The action whose program (or `handoff_when` check) runs; absent when no single action of the runbook's bindings binds the program.

case_id.description: The case the program runs for; absent when the runtime names none.

started_at.description: The `at` of the event `runbook.action-started` of this step.

seconds.description: Whole seconds from started_at to the moment the view is read, 0 or more.

sdc.decision.AutonomyLevel.title: AutonomyLevel
sdc.decision.AutonomyLevel.description: The run's autonomy level, docs/autonomy-levels.md:36-42 and :205-213: A0 Manual, A1 Advised, A2 Internal, A3 To merge, A4 To release, A5 Unattended (eval runs, :41-42). The level does not decide eligibility by itself: with the request's decision class it gives the holder (:241-256, overrides :297-320), and the guards read the holder.
